# Scientific review: pairwise-annihilating two-dimensional representations

## Correctness

**PASS.** A nonzero rank-one matrix is either nonnilpotent with complementary image and kernel, in which case its two-sided annihilator is one-dimensional and generated by the complementary projector, or square-zero with equal image and kernel, in which case its two-sided annihilator is its own line. This dichotomy exhausts all ordered mutual-zero-product tuples. The pair locus has a dense irreducible projector parametrization and an explicit degeneration capturing the nilpotent boundary. The all-nilpotent locus is the cone over a Segre–Veronese embedding, and distinct generic witnesses establish maximality. Exact-support counts establish the arithmetic identity. The packaged checker directly confirms 27 finite-field cases plus three exhaustive support stratifications. No general claim rests solely on finite experiments.

## Originality

**PASS, with residual priority risk.** The known two-matrix component classification appears explicitly in Schröer's archival 2002 paper; the existing general finite-field pair enumeration is covered by Huang (2021). Their pair results have been excluded from the novelty claim. Huisgen-Zimmermann and Goodearl (2011) develop general techniques for representation varieties of finite-dimensional algebras; their specific examples and general algorithms do not contain the explicit multibranch two-dimensional, all-arity classification here. Published mathematical record searches on mutually annihilating matrix tuples, complete cliques in mutual-annihilator graphs, and representations of a coordinate-axis fibre product did not locate a statement equivalent to the all-arity component count, first non-equidimensional arity, and higher-arity finite-field census. Prior work on tuples satisfying the stronger equations \(X_iX_j=0\) for **all** indices (including equal ones), and on cliques of nonzero square-zero matrices, covers the common-nilpotent sublocus but does not imply the full classification including single arbitrary matrices and complementary nonnilpotent projectors. The search cannot rule out an unindexed or differently phrased result, especially one about multiple-branch nodal singularities.

## Value

**PASS.** Two-dimensional representations of coordinate-axis fibre-product algebras are a natural test family for the geometry of module varieties; already the two-branch case appears in the established literature on product-zero matrix pairs. The full component classification detects a new geometric family that first becomes an irreducible component at arity three, and a strict dimension jump that first occurs at arity four. It also provides all finite-field point counts and a motivic formula from the same structural decomposition. These are not arbitrary finite cutoff computations and have direct use in understanding representation varieties and their zeta functions.

## Closest literature and limits

- Schröer, arXiv:math/0211293, introduction and Theorem 1.1: nilpotent and unrestricted **pairs**, not arbitrary-length tuples.
- Huang, arXiv:2110.15566, Theorem 1.2 and Section 3.1: finite-field enumeration of **pairs**, not higher tuples.
- Huisgen-Zimmermann and Goodearl, arXiv:1108.2833, Sections 1, 4–5: general module-variety techniques and other explicit examples, not this exact family.
- Crawley-Boevey and Schröer, arXiv:math/0103100, introduction: broad module-variety framework, without the explicit component counts here.

Results concern reduced varieties over arbitrary fields, with no assertion about nonreduced structures, higher-dimensional representations or isomorphism-orbit classification. Historical publication-priority searches do not constitute independent certification.

Self-review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.
